subject: Inference plane boundary walkthrough with BrightGrid
messages:
From: Aria Singh <aria.singh@brightgrid.com>
To: connor_obrien@redwood.ai, irene_choi@redwood.ai
Cc: edgeops@brightgrid.com
Date: 2028-03-15T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Walkthrough: inference-plane boundary & ops handoff (proposed)

Hi Connor / Irene,

Thanks again for the time last week. As we get closer to BrightGrid's private deployment cutover, the engineering and edge-ops teams asked for a short architecture walkthrough focused on the inference plane boundary: where the orchestration/control services sit versus the data/serving fabric in their VPCs.

Attached is a first-cut diagram (inference_boundary_diagram_v1.pdf) that highlights the public/private demarcation, the proposed egress proxies, and where KMS will be terminated. We'd like to validate the following during the call:

- Clarify which ports and protocols we expect for runtime RPCs between the Redwood control endpoint and on-prem agents.
- Confirm expectations for KV/cache persistence and whether that remains within the tenant VPC or in a BrightGrid-only subnet.
- Walk through the proposed failover path if the preferred GPU pool is saturated (what model variants to fall back to and routing policy).
- Ops handoff: what runbook artifacts you need from BrightGrid to operate an initial rollout (we attached a skeleton ops runbook).

Proposed 45-min slot: Thu Mar 16 10:00-10:45 PT. If that works for your team, we'll send calendar invites and a short agenda.

Looking forward —
Aria
Edge Solutions Architect
BrightGrid

[attachment: inference_boundary_diagram_v1.pdf (diagram, 1 page)]

From: connor_obrien@redwood.ai
To: Aria Singh <aria.singh@brightgrid.com>
Cc: irene_choi@redwood.ai, marcus_lin@redwood.ai, neha_kapoor@redwood.ai
Date: 2028-03-15T12:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Walkthrough: inference-plane boundary & ops handoff (proposed)

Aria —

Thu 10:00 PT works for us. Thanks for the diagram; quick read-through below and a couple of asks so the session is productive:

High level notes:
- The separation you show between orchestration (control) and serving (data/inference) is what we expect. We're going to refer to the two as the orchestration plane and the inference plane during the call.
- For runtime RPCs, we prefer mTLS over a single east-west port range (we'll propose 7000-7010 for inter-agent control). Can BrightGrid confirm whether those ports can be opened intra-VPC between the control endpoint and on-prem agents?
- KV/cache: we need clarity on LRU persistence. If BrightGrid wants local caching per-tenant, we need a clear eviction and warmup plan to avoid cold-start token spikes.

Asks before the meeting:
1) Aria — can you add a short table to the diagram PDF that lists which subnets are customer-managed vs. BrightGrid-managed? That avoids ambiguity when we propose subnet-level ACLs.
2) Irene — please bring the initial runbook template and a shortlist of the operational checks we expect to gate production cutover.
3) Marcus — can you prepare the fallback model mapping (which quantized variant we fall back to when preferred instance types are unavailable)?

I'll draft a rough agenda and send the invite to the attendees you listed.

Connor O'Brien
Principal Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference

[inline note: referencing attachment 'inference_boundary_diagram_v1.pdf']

From: irene_choi@redwood.ai
To: connor_obrien@redwood.ai, Aria Singh <aria.singh@brightgrid.com>
Cc: neha_kapoor@redwood.ai
Date: 2028-03-16T08:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Walkthrough: inference-plane boundary & ops handoff (proposed)

On Thu, Mar 15, 2028 at 12:05 PM Connor O'Brien <connor_obrien@redwood.ai> wrote:
> Aria —
>
> Thu 10:00 PT works for us. Thanks for the diagram; quick read-through below and a couple of asks so the session is productive:

Thanks — putting together the runbook draft now (attached as ops_runbook_draft.md). For the call I will:

- Bring a short cutover checklist (preflight tests, health probes, circuit-breaker settings).
- Walk through the expected observability hooks we will require (span tagging for tenant_id, token-level cost traces, and an alert for KV-hit-rate drops).
- Propose a minimal rollback plan: immediate traffic diversion to a hosted fallback with documented timeout thresholds.

Two clarifying points for BrightGrid before we meet:
1) Can you confirm whether BrightGrid requires HSM-backed KMS (customer key in BrightGrid KMS) vs. Redwood-managed keys? That affects how we design the control-plane TLS termination.
2) For egress proxying, do you need an explicit NAT Gateway per tenant, or is a shared outbound proxy acceptable for the initial pilot?

I attached a draft of the runbook and a small JSON snippet with typical healthcheck responses (annotated_infra_snippets.json).

Irene Choi
SRE Manager | Redwood Inference

[attachment: ops_runbook_draft.md (markdown, 4 pages)]
[attachment: annotated_infra_snippets.json (example payloads)]

From: marcus_lin@redwood.ai
To: connor_obrien@redwood.ai, irene_choi@redwood.ai, Aria Singh <aria.singh@brightgrid.com>
Cc: neha_kapoor@redwood.ai
Date: 2028-03-17T16:32:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Walkthrough: inference-plane boundary & ops handoff (proposed)

Great session today — thanks everyone. Summary and agreed next steps (assignments follow):

Summary:
- Agreed boundary: orchestration plane endpoints live in a BrightGrid-managed control subnet with strict mTLS restricted ports; inference plane (serving) lives in tenant-managed subnets.
- KV/cache: tenant-local cache accepted for pilot; eviction policy TTL=20m, with a warmup prefetch on deployment. Production expectation: move metadata-only indices to BrightGrid-managed cache to reduce cross-VPC latency.
- Fallbacks: Redwood will provide a quantized-variant mapping (Marcus action item) and a hosted fallback route for immediate rollback.
- Keys: BrightGrid prefers customer-managed KMS (HSM). We'll need an integration pattern note in the runbook.

Action items (owners & ETA):
- Marcus Lin: publish fallback mapping and a small compatibility matrix (INFR-3245) by 2028-03-21.
- Neha Kapoor: produce annotated network diagram that tags ACLs and proposed security group rules; drop into the shared Drive folder and ping Aria by 2028-03-20.
- Aria / BrightGrid: add subnet ownership table to the diagram and confirm whether a shared outbound proxy is OK for pilot by 2028-03-19.
- Connor: consolidate today's call notes into the confluence checklist and open the cutover ticket.

Neha — please pick up the network diagram task and use the sample ACL templates in the Ops runbook draft. Marcus — I'll worked with you offline on the quantized mapping.

Marcus Lin
Head of Inference Ops | Redwood Inference
